submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad layer-0 head that forwards whichever earlier token wins its attention (usually the previous token) and whose write deviates from its mean in proportion to that forwarded token: ordinary prose is weakly to moderately active (20 varied sentence peaks 0.86-2.49, all above the ~0.75 line), while peaks are maximal (2.2-3.1) when the forwarded token is an open-class/content word such as 'one', 'Mrs', 'addicted', 'Light' or 'energy', and collapse to or below the line when the forwarded token is a bleached function item ('of', 'to', 'is', 'in', 'a') — so the same peak token (e.g. ' of') ranges from ~0 to ~3.0 depending only on its predecessor.

rival_explanations: Exact-bigram 'one of' detector: fires only when 'of' immediately follows 'one', so 'Mrs.', 'addicted to', 'Light energy' and repeated 'and' should all be inactive.
Uniform function-word responder: every 'of' or 'to' peaks near the maximum regardless of its predecessor, so 'of of', 'to to' and 'one to' should all hit ~3.0.
